samples.xml_description:
<module id="div_8bit">
    <description>Implement a simplified radix-2 divider on 8-bit signed or unsigned integers. The module accepts a dividend and a divisor as inputs and provides a 16-bit result containing both the quotient and the remainder. The design supports both signed and unsigned division operations.</description>
    <ports>
        <input id="clk">Clock signal used for synchronous operation.</input>
        <input id="rst">The reset signal to initialize or reset the module.</input>
        <input id="sign">1-bit indicates if the operation is signed (1) or unsigned (0).</input>
        <input id="dividend" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the dividend for division.</input>
        <input id="divisor" width_description="[7:0]">8-bit input signal representing the divisor for division.</input>
        <input id="opn_valid">1-bit indicates that a valid operation request is present.</input>
        <input id="res_ready">1-bit indicates that the 16-bit output result has already been acknowledged.</input>
        <output id="res_valid">1-bit output signal indicating the result is valid and ready.</output>
        <output id="result" width_description="[15:0]">16-bit the output containing the remainder in the upper 8 bits and the quotient in the lower 8 bits.</output>
    </ports>
    <parameter_description>
        <parameter id="DIVIDE" value="1'b0">Indicates that the operation is a division.</parameter>
        <parameter id="MULTIPLY" value="1'b1">Indicates that the operation is a multiplication.</parameter>
    </parameter_description>
    <logic_description type="sequential_logic">
        <reg id="res_valid_reg" init_value="1'b0">Register to hold the result validity status.</reg>
        <reg id="start_cnt" init_value="1'b0">Register to indicate the start of the division process.</reg>
        <reg id="cnt" init_value="1'b0">Counter to keep track of the number of iterations.</reg>
        <reg id="neg_divisor" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="[7:0]0">Register to store the negative value of the divisor.</reg>
        <reg id="remainder" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="[7:0]0">Register to store the remainder.</reg>
        <reg id="quotient" width_description="[7:0]" init_value="[7:0]0">Register to store the quotient.</reg>
        <reg id="SR" width_description="[15:0]" init_value="[15:0]0">Shift Register to store the dividend during the division process.</reg>
        
        // Combinational Logic
        <always_comb>
            <if condition="!rst && !res_valid_reg && opn_valid">
                <assign dividend_abs = (sign == DIVIDE && dividend[7]) ? (~dividend + 1) : dividend;
                <assign divisor_abs = (sign == DIVIDE && divisor[7]) ? (~divisor + 1) : divisor;
                
                <assign remainder = dividend_abs;
                <assign quotient = 0;
                <assign SR = {dividend_abs, 1'b0};
                <assign neg_divisor = ~divisor_abs + 1;
            </if>
            
            <else_if condition="start_cnt">
                <if condition="cnt[7]">
                    <assign cnt = 0;
                    <assign start_cnt = 0;
                    
                    <assign SR = {remainder, quotient};
                </if>
                else begin
                    <assign cnt = cnt + 1;
                    <assign remainder = remainder - neg_divisor;
                    <assign quotient = quotient << 1;
                    <assign quotient[cnt] = (remainder >= 0);
                    <assign remainder = (remainder >= 0) ? remainder : remainder + divisor_abs;
                end
            </else>
        </always_comb>
        
        // Sequential Logic
        <always_ff posedge clk or posedge rst>
            <if condition="rst">
                <assign res_valid_reg <= 0;
            </else_if>
            <else_if condition="cnt == 8 || res_ready">
                <assign res_valid_reg <= 0;
            </else_if>
            <else>
                <assign res_valid_reg <= res_valid_reg;
            </else>
        </always_ff>
    </logic_description>
    
    <implementation>
        When opn_valid is high and res_valid is low, the module saves the inputs dividend and divisor.
        Initializes the shift register SR with the absolute value of the dividend shifted left by one bit.
        Sets NEG_DIVISOR to the negated absolute value of the divisor.
        Sets the counter cnt to 1 and start_cnt to 1 to begin the division process.
        Division Process(If start_cnt is high, the module performs the following steps):
        If the counter cnt reaches 8 (most significant bit of cnt is set), the division is complete:
        cnt and start_cnt are cleared.
        Updates the shift register SR with the final remainder and quotient.
        Otherwise, the counter cnt is incremented, and the shift register SR is updated based on the subtraction result:
        Computes the subtraction of NEG_DIVISOR.
        Uses a multiplexer to select the appropriate result based on the carry-out.
        Updates SR by shifting left and inserting the carry-out.
        Result Validity:
        res_valid is managed based on the reset signal, the counter, and whether the result has been consumed.
        res_valid should be update directly, without passing middle register value.
        res_valid is set to zero if rst is high.
        Otherwise, if cnt reaches 8, res_ready is set to 1.
        Otherwise, if res_valid and res_ready is all high, res_valid is set to 0.
        Otherwise, res_valid is set to res_valid.
    </implementation>
</module>
